_comment: Hand-written facts. Keys are ISO 3166 alpha-3 codes. Anything not listed here still gets facts worked out from data/live.json. Record sources: use 'Guinness World Records' only when Guinness itself recognises the record; otherwise 'Widely cited'. Guinness has no open data feed, so these are not refreshed automatically. Check them yourself.
world: Around 71 percent of Earth's surface is water, but only about 3 percent of that water is fresh.
There are more than 7,000 living languages, and roughly 40 percent of them are endangered.
The Pacific Ocean is larger than all of Earth's land put together.
Antarctica holds about 70 percent of the world's fresh water, locked in ice.
Africa has 54 countries recognised by the United Nations, more than any other continent.
The world's population passed 8 billion in November 2022, according to the United Nations.
Mount Everest, on the border of Nepal and China, is Earth's highest mountain above sea level at 8,849 metres.
Lake Baikal in Russia is the deepest lake on Earth, at about 1,640 metres.
The shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest point on dry land on Earth, more than 430 metres below sea level.
Mandarin has the most native speakers of any language, while English is spoken by the most people in total.
Indonesia and the Philippines together have more than 24,000 islands.
Vatican City, at about 0.44 square kilometres, is the smallest country in the world.

ISR.fun: The shore of the Dead Sea, more than 430 metres below sea level, is the lowest point on dry land on Earth.
ISR.special: Hebrew, kept alive for centuries mainly in prayer and writing, was revived as an everyday spoken language and is now spoken by millions of people.
known: Jerusalem holds sites sacred to Judaism, Christianity and Islam, including the Western Wall, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre and the Dome of the Rock.
The Dead Sea Scrolls, some of the oldest known manuscripts of the Hebrew Bible, were found in caves near the Dead Sea between 1947 and 1956.

records.text: Lowest point on dry land on Earth (Dead Sea shore)

JPN.fun: Nishiyama Onsen Keiunkan, a hot-spring inn in the mountains of Yamanashi, has welcomed guests since the year 705.
JPN.special: Hanami, the custom of gathering under cherry blossoms each spring, turns parks into picnics from Okinawa to Hokkaido.
known: Mount Fuji, at 3,776 metres, is the highest mountain in Japan.
Shinkansen bullet trains began running between Tokyo and Osaka in 1964.

records.text: Nishiyama Onsen Keiunkan, open since 705, is the world's oldest hotel

EGY.fun: The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest human-made structure in the world for roughly 3,800 years.
EGY.special: Ancient Egyptians wrote in hieroglyphs, and the Rosetta Stone, found in 1799, helped scholars finally read them.
known: Most Egyptians live in a narrow strip along the Nile and its delta.
The Suez Canal, opened in 1869, links the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea.

records.text: Great Pyramid of Giza: tallest human-made structure for about 3,800 years

IND.fun: Chess grew out of an Indian game called chaturanga, played more than 1,400 years ago.
IND.special: Indian mathematicians developed the decimal place-value system and treated zero as a number in its own right.
known: Hindi and English are the official languages of the national government, and the constitution lists 22 scheduled languages.
Indian Railways is one of the largest rail networks in the world.

CHN.fun: Paper, printing, gunpowder and the compass are known as China's Four Great Inventions.
CHN.special: The Spring Festival travel rush, called chunyun, is often described as the largest yearly human migration.
known: The Great Wall is a series of walls built by different dynasties over more than two thousand years.
China spans five geographic time zones but uses a single official time, Beijing time.

USA.fun: Yellowstone, established in 1872, is widely regarded as the world's first national park.
USA.special: Jazz, blues, rock and roll and hip-hop all grew out of American communities and have spread across the world.
known: Alaska and Hawaii became the 49th and 50th states in 1959.
The Grand Canyon in Arizona is about 446 kilometres long and up to about 1.8 kilometres deep.

BRA.fun: Brazil holds about 60 percent of the Amazon rainforest, the largest tropical rainforest on Earth.
BRA.special: Carnival in Rio de Janeiro, with its samba parades, is one of the biggest festivals in the world.
known: Portuguese is the official language, and Brazil is the only Portuguese-speaking country in South America.
Brasília, the capital, was built in the late 1950s and inaugurated in 1960.

records.text: Amazon rainforest: largest tropical rainforest on Earth

RUS.fun: Russia spans eleven time zones, from Kaliningrad in the west to Kamchatka in the east.
RUS.special: Lake Baikal in Siberia holds roughly a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water.
known: The Trans-Siberian Railway runs about 9,300 kilometres from Moscow to Vladivostok.
Russia borders more countries than almost any other nation.

records.text: Lake Baikal is the deepest lake on Earth, at about 1,640 metres

CAN.fun: Canada has the longest coastline of any country, at more than 200,000 kilometres including its islands.
CAN.special: Canada has two official languages, English and French, and Nunavut became an Inuit-majority territory in 1999.
known: Canada has more lakes than any other country, by most counts.
Most Canadians live within a few hours of the southern border.

AUS.fun: The Great Barrier Reef stretches for about 2,300 kilometres and is the largest coral reef system in the world.
AUS.special: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have lived on the continent for at least 50,000 years.
known: Uluru, a huge sandstone monolith in the Northern Territory, is sacred to the Anangu people.
Australia is a country that covers a whole continent.

records.text: Great Barrier Reef: largest coral reef system in the world

ZAF.fun: South Africa has three capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.
ZAF.special: South Africa has twelve official languages, including South African Sign Language.
known: Table Mountain, with its flat top, overlooks Cape Town.
Nelson Mandela became president in 1994, after the first fully democratic elections.

KEN.fun: Every year more than a million wildebeest cross between Tanzania's Serengeti and Kenya's Maasai Mara in the Great Migration.
KEN.special: Runners from Kenya's Rift Valley highlands have dominated distance racing for decades.
known: Mount Kenya, at 5,199 metres, is the second-highest mountain in Africa.
Swahili and English are the official languages.

ETH.fun: Ethiopia is considered the birthplace of coffee, and the coffee ceremony is still a daily ritual.
ETH.special: Ethiopia has its own calendar with 13 months, and it runs about seven to eight years behind the Gregorian calendar.
known: Lucy, a 3.2-million-year-old fossil skeleton of an early human relative, was found in the Afar region in 1974.
Ethiopia was never colonised, apart from a short Italian occupation from 1936 to 1941.

NGA.fun: Nollywood, Nigeria's film industry, is one of the largest in the world by number of films made each year.
NGA.special: More than 500 languages are spoken in Nigeria.
known: Abuja became the capital in 1991, replacing Lagos.
Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa.

MAR.fun: The University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, founded in 859, is recognised as the oldest continually operating university in the world.
MAR.special: Mint tea poured from a height is the traditional sign of welcome in Morocco.
known: The old medina of Fez, Fes el-Bali, is one of the largest car-free urban areas in the world.
Morocco recognises both Arabic and Tamazight as official languages.

records.text: University of al-Qarawiyyin (859): oldest existing, continually operating educational institution

TUR.fun: Göbekli Tepe in southeastern Turkey, built about 11,000 years ago, is among the oldest known monumental structures.
TUR.special: Istanbul sits on two continents, split by the Bosphorus strait.
known: Turkey is one of the world's largest producers of hazelnuts.
Ankara, not Istanbul, has been the capital since 1923.

IRN.fun: Qanats, underground channels that carry water from mountains to farms and towns, have supplied Iranian settlements for around 3,000 years.
IRN.special: Nowruz, the Persian New Year, is celebrated at the spring equinox and has been marked for more than 3,000 years.
known: Persepolis, begun by Darius I around 518 BCE, was a ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire.
Persian poets such as Hafez, Rumi and Ferdowsi are read around the world.

ARE.fun: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai rises 828 metres, taller than any other building ever completed.
ARE.special: Falconry is a traditional Emirati practice, and falcons even have their own hospitals and passports.
known: The UAE is a federation of seven emirates, including Abu Dhabi and Dubai.
Abu Dhabi is the capital, and Dubai is the largest city.

records.text: Burj Khalifa (828 m): tallest building in the world

ITA.fun: Two countries lie entirely inside Italy: San Marino and Vatican City.
ITA.special: The University of Bologna, founded in 1088, is often named as the oldest university in the Western world.
known: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than almost any other country.
Italy was unified as a single kingdom in 1861.

FRA.fun: France is regularly one of the most visited countries in the world.
FRA.special: The traditional French gastronomic meal is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.
known: The Louvre in Paris is one of the most visited museums in the world.
France has more time zones than any other country when its overseas territories are counted.

DEU.fun: Johannes Gutenberg's movable-type printing press, developed in Mainz around 1450, helped spread printed books across Europe.
DEU.special: Christmas markets, a tradition going back to the late Middle Ages, are held in towns and cities across Germany every winter.
known: The Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989, and Germany reunified in 1990.
Germany shares borders with nine countries.

GBR.fun: The United Kingdom has no single written constitution document. It rests on laws, court decisions and long-standing conventions.
GBR.special: The Magna Carta of 1215 limited the power of the king and became a symbol of the rule of law.
known: The country is made up of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
Big Ben is the nickname of the great bell in the Elizabeth Tower at Westminster.

ISL.fun: Iceland's national assembly, the Althing, was founded in 930 and is one of the oldest parliaments in the world.
ISL.special: Most Icelanders use patronymics instead of family names, so a person's surname is based on their father's (or mother's) first name.
known: Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where two tectonic plates pull apart.
Nearly all of its electricity comes from renewable sources, mainly hydropower and geothermal energy.

records.text: Althing (930): one of the world's oldest parliaments

FIN.fun: Finland has roughly three million saunas for about 5.6 million people.
FIN.special: For decades, expecting mothers in Finland have received a maternity package that includes a cardboard box that can be used as a baby's first bed.
known: Finland has nearly 190,000 lakes.
Finnish and Swedish are the two official languages.

NLD.fun: About a quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level, protected by dikes, dunes and pumping stations.
NLD.special: Much of the Dutch countryside is polder, land reclaimed from the sea or from lakes.
known: Amsterdam is built on wooden piles driven into soft ground.
The Netherlands has more bicycles than people, by most estimates.

GRC.fun: Greece has more than 6,000 islands and islets, but fewer than 250 of them are inhabited.
GRC.special: Ancient Athens developed an early form of democracy around 508 BCE.
known: The Parthenon on the Acropolis in Athens was built in the 5th century BCE.
The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896.

CHL.fun: Chile stretches about 4,300 kilometres from north to south but averages less than 200 kilometres wide.
CHL.special: The Atacama Desert in northern Chile is one of the driest places on Earth.
known: Easter Island, known for its giant moai statues, belongs to Chile.
Chile is one of the world's biggest producers of copper.

records.text: Atacama Desert: driest non-polar desert on Earth

PER.fun: Peru has thousands of native potato varieties, around 4,000 by some counts.
PER.special: Machu Picchu, built by the Inca in the 15th century, sits high in the Andes at about 2,400 metres.
known: Spanish and Quechua are both official languages, and Aymara is official in some regions.
The Amazon River begins in the Peruvian Andes, according to many geographers.

MEX.fun: Chocolate, chillies, maize and tomatoes all trace back to the peoples of Mesoamerica.
MEX.special: Día de Muertos, the Day of the Dead, is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.
known: Mexico City was built on the site of Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital, traditionally founded in 1325.
Mexico recognises 68 national indigenous languages alongside Spanish.

BTN.fun: Bhutan absorbs more carbon dioxide than it releases, which makes it carbon negative.
BTN.special: Bhutan measures its progress with Gross National Happiness, not just income.
known: Thimphu is often cited as one of the few capital cities in the world without traffic lights.
Bhutan's name for itself is Druk Yul, the Land of the Thunder Dragon.

NPL.fun: Nepal's flag is the only national flag in the world that is not a rectangle or square.
NPL.special: Lumbini, in southern Nepal, is traditionally regarded as the birthplace of the Buddha.
known: Eight of the world's fourteen mountains over 8,000 metres lie wholly or partly in Nepal.
Kathmandu sits in a valley at about 1,400 metres above sea level.

records.text: Mount Everest (8,849 m, on the Nepal–China border): highest mountain above sea level

MNG.fun: Mongolia has the lowest population density of any sovereign country, with a lot of land for each person.
MNG.special: Naadam, a festival of wrestling, archery and horse racing, is held every July.
known: Genghis Khan founded the Mongol Empire in 1206.
Many Mongolians still live a nomadic life, moving with their herds in felt tents called gers.

NZL.fun: New Zealand has far more sheep than people.
NZL.special: In 1893, New Zealand became the first self-governing country to give women the vote in national elections.
known: Aotearoa is the Māori name for New Zealand.
Te reo Māori and New Zealand Sign Language are official languages, and English is the most widely used.

records.text: First self-governing country to give women the vote in national elections (1893)

MCO.fun: Monaco is the most densely populated sovereign country in the world, with tens of thousands of people in about two square kilometres.
MCO.special: The Monaco Grand Prix is raced on the city's own streets every year.
known: Monaco is the second-smallest country in the world, after Vatican City.
Monaco is surrounded by France on land and has a coastline on the Mediterranean.

SGP.fun: Singapore is both a city and a country, a city-state with about 6 million people on one island and a few dozen small ones.
SGP.special: Singapore has four official languages: English, Malay, Mandarin and Tamil.
known: Singapore became an independent country in 1965.
Singapore's name comes from the Malay Singapura, meaning Lion City.

IDN.fun: Indonesia is made up of more than 17,000 islands, which makes it the world's largest island country.
IDN.special: Around 700 languages are spoken across Indonesia.
known: Komodo dragons, the largest living lizards, live on a few Indonesian islands.
Indonesia lies on the Ring of Fire and has more than a hundred active volcanoes.

records.text: Largest island country in the world

PHL.fun: The Philippines has more than 7,600 islands.
PHL.special: The Philippines is the largest Christian-majority country in Asia.
known: Filipino and English are the official languages.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Luzon have been farmed for hundreds of years.

KOR.fun: South Korea moved to the international system of counting age in June 2023, so people are no longer a year or two older on paper.
KOR.special: Chuseok, the autumn harvest festival, is one of the biggest holidays, when families travel home and share songpyeon rice cakes.
known: The Korean Peninsula has been divided since 1945, and the border zone is called the Demilitarized Zone.
Hangul, the Korean alphabet, was created in the 1440s.

THA.fun: Thailand is often described as the only country in Southeast Asia that was never colonised by a European power.
THA.special: Songkran, the Thai New Year in April, is celebrated with water fights in the streets.
known: Bangkok's ceremonial name is one of the longest place names for any capital city.
Thailand was called Siam until 1939.

COL.fun: Colombia is home to more bird species than any other country, about 1,900.
COL.special: The Coffee Cultural Landscape in the Andes is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
known: Colombia has coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.
Colombia is one of the world's biggest producers of coffee.

records.text: Most bird species of any country

ARG.fun: Aconcagua in Argentina, at 6,961 metres, is the highest mountain outside Asia.
ARG.special: Tango, born in the port districts of Buenos Aires and Montevideo, is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.
known: Argentina and Chile share the longest border in South America.
Patagonia, in the far south, is shared with Chile.

VAT.fun: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, with an area of about 0.44 square kilometres.
VAT.special: Vatican City has its own post office, stamps, radio station and newspaper.
known: The Pope is the head of state, and the Swiss Guard has protected popes since 1506.
Vatican City lies entirely within the city of Rome.

records.text: Smallest country in the world by area and population

TWN.fun: Taipei 101 was the tallest building in the world from 2004 until 2010.
TWN.special: Night markets are a big part of daily life in Taiwan, with street food stalls open late into the evening.
known: Mandarin is the main language, alongside Taiwanese Hokkien, Hakka and Indigenous languages.
Taiwan is a leading maker of computer chips.

records.text: Taipei 101 was the world's tallest building from 2004 to 2010
